title: Single-Orchestrator Parallel Mission Delivery: Evaluate the Upstream Orchestration Skills and Build the Sanctuary Mission Orchestrator
target_platform: Claude Code, Codex and Antigravity CLIs as parallel workers in git worktrees; globally installed orchestrating-agent-work and cli-agent skills (APM); Sanctuary flight board
hypothesis: A Sanctuary mission-orchestrator skill, a thin wrapper over the globally installed orchestrating-agent-work skill that adds (a) mission selection by priority and independence, (b) dispatch of up to 3 missions in parallel to 3 different CLIs, each in its own leased worktree, (c) independent review and scoring of each delivery against its falsifiable promises, (d) a continuously improving evaluation rubric, and (e) orchestrator-run merging in dependency order including ID allocation and recompilation of generated files, delivers a pilot batch of 3 missions with: wall-clock <= 60% of running the same missions sequentially; 0 file clobbering and <= 1 conflict-resolution round per PR; orchestrator token overhead <= 25% of the workers' total; review scores within +/-1 of an independent re-score on >= 80% of dimensions; and >= 1 genuine delivery defect caught that the worker's self-score missed.
falsification_criteria: Any pilot threshold missed (wall-clock > 60% of sequential, clobbering or > 1 conflict round per PR, token overhead > 25%, review agreement < 80%, zero defects caught); or one worker corrupts another's worktree or files; or an orchestrator-run merge leaves main failing its tests; or the orchestrator merges, pushes or signs anything without the human approval its policy requires; or Phase 1 shows the existing upstream skill already covers selection, dispatch, review and merge with configuration alone (then no new skill is warranted and the result is recorded as such).
phases: P1 Evaluate the upstream orchestration skills (SKILL.md plus references: Graph/DAG, Dual-Loop, Parallel Swarm, Red-Team Review, topology rules, routing and closure, CLI-agent executor) with a written rubric: mission selection, worktree confinement, parallel dispatch to different CLIs, delivery review against falsifiable promises, merge handling, human gates; list the gaps.

P2 Design the Sanctuary wrapper skill in plugins/sanctuary-core (generic gaps go upstream under Protocol 133); define the policies: merge authority, reviewer independence, resource scheduling, ID and generated-file ownership.

P3 Pilot (after MISSION-031, or with manual --targets): 3 low-risk missions in parallel on 3 CLIs in leased worktrees; baseline = the same work done sequentially and the 2026-11-03/04 two-agent session metrics.
P4 Independent re-score of every delivery by a different vendor than the worker; compare with the orchestrator's review and the workers' self-scores.
P5 Record the result, feed rubric improvements back into the evaluation skill, replenish the backlog.
design_constraints: Human Gate: the orchestrator prepares commits, PRs and merges but only performs them under the approval policy the human sets per batch; it never self-signs manifests (upstream rule).
Reviewer independence: the reviewer of a delivery is a different vendor than its worker where possible.
Resource scheduling: at most one mission that loads the local 7B model at a time on a 16 GB machine (flight-board resource lock).
Orchestrator owns mission and chronicle ID allocation, merge order, regeneration of index.jsonl/backlog.md, and reconciliation of ledger aggregates.
Inner worker loops never run git write commands; commits and merges stay with the caller (upstream Loop Isolation).
Consume MISSION-031's projected_impact and overlap matrix for mission independence and lease targets; the orchestrator adds selection policy and review, not a second collision detector.

Usage and budget awareness: before dispatching workers, the orchestrator checks backend headroom (5-hour and weekly windows) through MISSION-035's probe and treats a nearly exhausted window as a hard constraint on worker assignment; after completion it records measured deltas, not estimates, once 035 is available.
baseline_evidence: Two-agent session 2026-11-03/04 (Claude Code and Antigravity in parallel worktrees): collisions and reconciliation work the orchestrator would own: mission IDs 030/031 and chronicle 355 allocated concurrently; index.jsonl, backlog.md and the cognitive ledger collide on merge; one agent's score existed only as an uncommitted edit in the main tree and its events entry was never committed; manage_coordination checkout dirties the main tree and breaks git pull; merge order mattered (agy merged first). All scores were self-assessed.

model_routing.frontier_escalation_condition: The orchestrator and the independent reviewer run on a frontier model; escalate workers only for missions the orchestrator marks high-risk.

related_missions.MISSION-031: DEPENDS ON: projected_impact declarations and the flight-board overlap matrix are the orchestrator's input for choosing independent missions and acquiring exact leases; do not build a second overlap detector. Land 031 first or run the pilot with manual --targets.
related_missions.MISSION-026: BUILDS ON (corroborated): flight board, leases and worktree isolation are the coordination substrate.
related_missions.MISSION-025: BUILDS ON: workers' checkin --handoff notes are read by the orchestrator during review and carried into the next batch.
related_missions.MISSION-032: INFORMED BY: shows which incoming agents (frontier vs local) reliably follow a briefing, which informs worker routing.
related_missions.MISSION-028: INFORMED BY: signal-triggered escalation policy for choosing a cheaper or stronger worker.
related_missions.MISSION-035: PROVIDER: measured usage telemetry (before/after token and quota-window snapshots, per-task-class cost predictor, headroom check). The orchestrator calls its snapshot and recommend commands for worker assignment and to measure its own token overhead; do not build a second usage tracker. Until 035 lands, the pilot records usage manually via track_budget.py.

projected_impact.basis: Declared 2026-11-04 by claude-code (MISSION-031 backfill) from the mission's hypothesis; a mission always also edits its own manifest. Refine at checkout and confirm with `manage_coordination.py verify`.
